Package org.rapidcow.trivnote.libexpr

Class Scalar

java.lang.Object
org.rapidcow.trivnote.libexpr.Datum
org.rapidcow.trivnote.libexpr.Atom
org.rapidcow.trivnote.libexpr.Scalar
Direct Known Subclasses:
BoolScalar, NumberScalar, StringScalar
public abstract sealed class Scalar extends Atom permits BoolScalar, NumberScalar, StringScalar
A boolean, number, or string Atom. The Atom.value() of a boolean or number is its wire representation. A string’s value is its unescaped content, without surrounding quotes.

A Scalar is one of three values: boolean, #t (BoolScalar.TRUE) and #f (BoolScalar.FALSE); free-form strings (via ofString(String)); and numbers (via ofNumber(String)).

Scalars are compared by Atom.value() for equality with the sole exception of strings, which can be distinguished using isString(). The reason is that while the value of a string scalar is an unescaped string, the value of a non-string scalar corresponds to its wire representation. In other words non-string scalars are the only datums who own serialization logic outside of DataDumper.

      public static NumberScalar ofNumber(String value)
      Returns an immutable numeric scalar atom.

      Usage: 

      Scalar v = Scalar.ofNumber("17/29");
      If you need to access number-specific fields, declare your variable with the type NumberScalar.
